clue.text: See 2
Scrubber turns up with quiet types

indicators.note: turns tells us to flip the little word up end to end

parts.note: taken as written before turning
mice are proverbially quiet, as in quiet as a mouse

explanation.surface: A cleaner arrives with some timid people in tow.
explanation.definitionFit: Volcanic stone of this kind is used as an abrasive for scrubbing hard skin.

clue.text: Work of slaves, damned

definitions.meaning: gathering the crop on American plantations was forced labour done by enslaved people
an American slang intensifier meaning blasted or confounded

explanation.surface: A grim comment on plantation labour, cursed work.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names plantation field labour and is also a folksy American expletive meaning blasted.

clue.text: Where immigrants come to see pitch

definitions.meaning: read as '...', the place immigrants arrive
the rise and fall of the voice in speaking, or accuracy of musical pitch

explanation.surface: A remark about arrivals heading somewhere to see a sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Intonation is the musical pitch of speech or accuracy in hitting notes.

clue.text: Relish rush over love

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece sits over (above) the next

parts.note: a gust is a sudden rush of wind
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Enjoyment comes in a rush when you're in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment, a synonym of relish in the sense of zest.

clue.text: Shook head in retreat, drained

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word bow is read in reverse

parts.note: the bow is the head or front end of a ship
bled means drained of blood or fluid

explanation.surface: Someone shook their head while backing off, utterly exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns BOW into WOB; 'head' is not a body part here but a ship's front.
explanation.definitionFit: To wobble is to shake unsteadily, so shook and wobbled are past-tense synonyms.

clue.text: Steeplechase obstacle appears right after a wet false start

indicators.note: R is placed after the anagrammed letters
a false version of the words is a rearranged one

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
to jump is to start in surprise

explanation.surface: In a horse race, a fence comes straight after a soggy false start.
explanation.definitionFit: A water jump is a fence with a pool beyond it, a classic hazard in steeplechase racing.

clue.text: Quickly eat duck in sandwich

indicators.note: in signals that one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a BLT is a bacon, lettuce and tomato sandwich
a duck in cricket is a score of zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Wolf down a sandwich with duck in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt food is to gulp it down hurriedly, a synonym for eating quickly.

clue.text: Noble term of address for Queen Mary, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: the form used when speaking to a peeress or titled woman
the Queen Mary was an ocean liner, and ships are traditionally called she

explanation.surface: How one should formally address Queen Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen Mary was a famous Cunard ocean liner; read as two words, a female vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the courteous title used for a titled woman, as in 'Her Ladyship'.

clue.text: Forcefully removing sulphur, one entering to remove smell?

indicators.note: entering tells us these two letters go inside the next piece

parts.note: pong is British slang for a stink, so de-pong would mean to take a stink away
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Getting rid of the sulphur, someone sets about deodorising.
explanation.walkthrough: PONG is British slang for a bad smell; DEPONG is a playful made-up verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Deposing a ruler is forcing them out of office, so the participles match.

clue.text: This composition is satisfied, having entered religious work

indicators.note: having entered places one piece inside the other

parts.note: met as in demands met, i.e. satisfied
OT is the Old Testament, a religious book

explanation.surface: A piece of music is approved after joining a sacred work.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short choral composition, typically sacred, so it is a kind of composition.

clue.text: Paid off debt and moved in to penthouse suite?

definitions.meaning: to settle up is to pay what one owes
read literally as settled high up, taking up residence at the top of a building

explanation.surface: Having cleared the bill, a person moves into a top-floor flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling up means paying a bill in full; read literally it means making a home up high.

clue.text: Line taken by failed con, in short was dealt with here?

definitions.text: Line taken by failed con, in short was dealt with here?

indicators.note: in places the run of letters inside the word for short

parts.note: curt means short or brusque

indicators.note: the line is followed by the next piece

parts.note: a row is a line

indicators.note: a failed version of the word con is a scrambled one

explanation.surface: A conman, briefly, ended up being tried at a criminal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' scrambles the word con; the line and that scramble sit inside the word for short just after its first letter. Read whole, the clue also describes where a failed conman is tried.
explanation.definitionFit: This English court tries serious criminal cases, the place where a convict would be dealt with.

clue.text: Relative introduces herself as goddess

indicators.note: the speaker's letter comes first, introducing the relative

parts.note: the clue speaks as herself, the first person I
sis is short for sister, a relative

explanation.surface: A family member presents herself as a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was a major goddess of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Chests are revealed to contain shilling — journalist fed up

indicators.note: the outer phrase is made to hold the other letters inside

parts.note: with bras off, chests are uncovered
S was the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A tabloid journalist, tired of it all, exposes topless pictures for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated S.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassed off is British slang for annoyed or fed up.

clue.text: This is a rag I hunted out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are worked out into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes the newspaper they found as a rag they tracked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges A RAG I HUNTED. 'This' is the newspaper in which the puzzle appeared, and rag is slang for a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle was printed in this newspaper, so 'this' points self-referentially at the paper.

clue.text: Beat up workers in sober performance

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word cane is read bottom to top

parts.note: to cane is to beat

indicators.note: in places the workers inside the abstainer's letters

parts.note: TT is teetotal, i.e. sober
men are workers

explanation.surface: Workers get roughed up during a staid show.
explanation.definitionFit: An enactment is an acting out of something, a performance.

clue.text: Charles carries home a wife — could this cause a messy separation?

definitions.text: could this cause a messy separation?

indicators.note: the name's abbreviation carries the next piece inside it

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A man brings his wife home, raising the prospect of a messy divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: This motorised cutting tool separates wood messily, scattering chips and sawdust.

clue.text: Second fast bowler, one out of this world

parts.note: in cricket a paceman is a fast bowler

explanation.surface: A cricket team's second quick bowler is out of this world.
explanation.walkthrough: A paceman bowls fast in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut leaves the earth, so they are literally out of this world.

clue.text: Some brain required, where the students wallow?

parts.note: read as a river beast's university grounds: a big wallowing animal plus a college site

explanation.surface: A brain region is needed where students lie around.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as two words: the beast that wallows plus the place students gather.
explanation.definitionFit: This seahorse-shaped structure is part of the brain involved in memory.

clue.text: Without a partner, one is released

definitions.meaning: a record put out on its own as a release

explanation.surface: Someone unattached is freed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means unmarried and is also a music track issued on its own.

clue.text: Country saying: "Me goose, ___"

indicators.note: saying signals that we listen to how the words sound

parts.note: the blank completes the saying with the male goose's name for 'you', as in me Tarzan, you Jane

explanation.surface: A goose introduces itself in a Tarzan-style phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The pattern is 'Me Tarzan, you Jane': the goose says 'Me goose, you gander', a gander being a male goose.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda is an East African nation.

clue.text: Livingstone couldn't stand the heat, which is irritating

indicators.note: from the saying 'if you can't stand the heat, get out of the kitchen', Livingstone gets out

parts.note: the kitchen is where the heat is in that saying
Ken Livingstone, former Mayor of London

explanation.surface: An explorer finds the heat unbearable, which annoys him.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests David Livingstone in Africa, but it is Ken Livingstone, ex-Mayor of London, leaving the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is an irritating sensation, so the noun fits 'which is irritating' loosely.

clue.text: Unbelievable performance of a drunkard?

explanation.surface: A drunk's routine is remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means astounding and also describes walking unsteadily, as a drunk does.

clue.text: Enormous scratch by the ear

indicators.note: judged by the ear means what matters is how it sounds

parts.note: to grate is to scrape or scratch

explanation.surface: A big scratch beside someone's ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Great means very large, a synonym for enormous.

clue.text: Bird or bard beginning to seem pale

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word gives one letter

parts.note: wan means pale

explanation.surface: A bird or poet starts looking peaky.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare was called the Swan of Avon.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large white bird, and Shakespeare is nicknamed the Swan of Avon.

clue.text: Homes were rebuilt without specific foundations

indicators.note: rebuilt means the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Houses were reconstructed with no proper foundations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges HOMES WERE; the definition means 'with no particular location'.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere means at an unspecified place, with no specific grounding or base.

clue.text: Ape's tail taken to heart — something like it

indicators.note: the last letter moves to the middle of the word

parts.note: an orang is an orangutan, an ape

explanation.surface: An ape takes its tail to heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart is one example, so 'something like it' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart is an organ, so the answer is something of the heart's kind.

clue.text: Such used to secure victory, having to draw about a quarter

parts.note: a win is a victory

indicators.note: the reversed word has the quarter letter inside it
about turns the word tug round

parts.note: to tug is to draw or pull
N, north, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Victory secured despite having to draw about a quarter of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TUG into GUT, then N goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing nut is a fastener with flat wings, used to secure bolts.

clue.text: Material of Welsh separatists?

parts.note: Taff is a slang name for a Welshman
ETA was the Basque separatist group

explanation.surface: A cloth of Welsh nationalists.
explanation.walkthrough: ETA was the Basque separatist group in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp woven fabric.
